land.text: Polotsk, held by Iziaslav of Polotsk's line when Yaroslav's lands were divided (the rus dossier, Kievan Rus' page); Cliopatria's first Polotsk shape is 1056

predecessors.note: The principality is far older: first mentioned in 862, ruled by Rogvolod in 980 and by Vseslav from 1044 (Polotsk pages); its infobox says 'Established: 862' and 'Preceded by: Kievan Rus''. The map starts it where the rus dossier ends.

land.text: Polotsk, a vassal of the Lithuanian princes from 1240 and annexed by Vytenis in 1307

successors.note: Cliopatria stops the Polotsk row in 1249 and its Lithuania shape covers the core from 1250 (163 of 164 cells); the pages keep the principality, as a vassal, to 1307.

capitals.name: Polotsk (Polatsk)
capitals.note: Infobox capital 'Polotsk'; the town was the principality's seat throughout, while the sons of Vseslav ruled Minsk, Vitebsk and Drutsk from 1101. Coordinates of the modern city.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the pages give Polotsk as an older principality (infobox 'Established: 862') and date no extent for 1054-1055; the keyframe bridges the rus dossier's 1054 hand-over to Cliopatria's first Polotsk shape in 1056 and assumes the 1056 shape. Confidence of the shape: 1.

103,984 km2 (1056-1084). The infobox gives 100,000-120,000 km2 for the principality 'at the time of its greatest extent' in 'northern and central Belarus': ratio 0.87-1.04, so the shape fits. The page dates no frontier of these years.

133,005 km2: the 1056 shape plus 137 cells (about 34,000 km2) to the west and north-west over Latgale (Daugavpils, Rezekne) and to Vilnius. The infobox area (100,000-120,000) puts it at 1.1-1.3 times, inside the factor of two, but no page opened dates or names that western reach. Years corrected: Polotsk was divided among Vseslav's sons after his death on 24 April 1101 (Vitebsk page: 'Polotsk was divided into six smaller principalities'), so this shape holds 1085-1100 only; Cliopatria draws it to 1110. Re-checked 2026-10-31: the 1101 splits (Minsk, Drutsk, Jersika, Koknese, and the Vitebsk fief) now account for the shape: the five Cliopatria shapes of 1111 cover 613 of its 619 cells, and the 137 cells added in 1085 are 108 Jersika, 10 Koknese and 15 Minsk (Jersika page: Jersika 'in the east bordering Polotsk'; Polotsk's tributary rights over it until 1212).

minus.text: the Vitebsk lands, a fief apart from 1101 to about 1195

correction.text: Polotsk proper: the 1202 core without the Vitebsk fief

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Polotsk row for 1111-1201 (and keeps the 133,005 km2 shape to 1110). After the 1101 division the town of Polotsk and its lands stayed with Davyd Vseslavich (Vseslav page: 'Davyd: Polotsk, and succeeded Vseslav there') while Vitebsk, Minsk and Drutsk went to other sons. The 1202 core without a 60 km disc round Vitebsk is the reading; the radius is mine, the Vitebsk fief is the page's. Cliopatria draws the whole 34,385 km2 core for 1111-1187 as 'Principality of Vitebsk'; the two dossiers overlap and the colour agent must choose. Confidence of the shape: 1. Size: 133 of the core's 164 cells (about 27,900 km2); the Vitebsk disc is the other 31 cells (about 6,500 km2). With the splits of 1101 (Minsk 52,681, Drutsk 19,978, Jersika 23,422, Koknese 2,162 km2 and the Vitebsk fief) it rebuilds the 133,005 km2 shape of 1085-1100. In 1129-1131 this land is Kiev's (loss 1129, gain 1132); Vitebsk is the fief's own land until the gain of 1195.

correction.text: Polotsk with the middle Dvina and the Vitebsk lands, Cliopatria's post-1202 shape (34,385 km2)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Vitebsk page says the princes who 'in 1195 marched against the prince of Smolensk' restored Vitebsk to Polotsk's rule, so Polotsk and Vitebsk are one again from 1195 and the 1202 core (34,385 km2) is the shape. Cliopatria leaves 1188-1201 to Smolensk (its 150,649 km2 shape of those years is the Smolensk shape plus these same 164 cells); the Vitebsk page has Smolensk's influence over Vitebsk from 1186 to 1195, not over Polotsk. The return of the Vitebsk fief is the gain of 1195 (counterpart principality-of-vitebsk).

34,385 km2. The infobox's 100,000-120,000 km2 is the greatest extent; this post-division core is 0.3 of it, beyond the factor of two but consistent with the fragmentation the page describes ('Polotsk was splintered between various smaller fiefs'). It includes both Polotsk and Vitebsk.
34,533 km2, +148 km2 on 1202: a redraw, no event on the pages opened. Same core.
34,488 km2, -44 km2 on 1210: a redraw, no event. The page has Polotsk a vassal of the Livonian Brothers of the Sword 1227-1240 and of Lithuania from 1240 without moving the core.

34,488 km2, the 1216 shape unchanged. The years are corrected: Cliopatria stops in 1249 and its Lithuania shape covers the core from 1250, but the pages keep the principality alive as a vassal of Lithuania from 1240 ('Polotsk became a vassal of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania' in 1240) and annexed by force by Vytenis in 1307 ('It officially became part of Lithuania in 1307, though it retained some degree of local autonomy until the 1390s'). The shape is held for 1241-1306.

region.text: Polotsk as Cliopatria draws it from 1056

ledger.note: 1054: Polotsk stands apart from the sons' division of Rus', the principality of the Vseslavichi's line. The page's infobox says 'Established: 862' (first mentioned in the Primary Chronicle), and 'In 980' its ruler was Rogvolod; the Vseslav page has Vseslav on the throne from 1044. The date 1054 is the end of the rus dossier, not a founding. Re-read 2026-10-31: the Polotsk (town) page says 'Its most powerful ruler was Prince Vseslav of Polotsk, who reigned from 1044 to 1101' and that the city 'repeatedly asserted its sovereignty in relation to other centers of Kievan Rus''; it does not address Yaroslav's 1054 division, so 1054 stays a bridge to the rus dossier (confidence 1).

region.text: Minsk, sacked by the Yaroslavichi before the Nemiga battle

ledger.note: 1067: the Yaroslavichi sack Minsk and defeat Vseslav on the Nemiga. 'defeating Vseslav in battle on the Nemiga River on March 3, 1067'; 'Before the battle, the Yaroslavichi sacked Minsk, which was then under Polotsk's control.' Vseslav was seized in June (year not stated, 1067 inferred) and held in Kiev.

region.text: Minsk and the Polotsk lands, secured by Vseslav

ledger.note: 1071: Vseslav holds Polotsk. 'he finally secured Polotsk in 1071,' after the Kiev uprising of 1068 freed him and made him grand prince (September 1068 - April 1069) and Iziaslav's return drove him back.

region.text: the western and north-western land (Latgale to Vilnius) Cliopatria adds in 1085

ledger.note: 1085: Cliopatria widens Polotsk to the west over Latgale and as far as Vilnius (+34,000 km2). No page opened dates this; the Vitebsk page has a 1106 raid by Sviatoslav of Vitebsk on the Baltic tribes in Semigallia, which shows reach but not rule. Kept as a bridge. Re-checked 2026-10-31: the Principality of Jersika page (infobox 'Preceded by: Principality of Polotsk') puts Jersika in Latgale, 'in the east bordering Polotsk', and says 'In 1212, Polotsk gave up its tributary rights over Jersika in favor of Bishop Albert', so Latgale was a Polotsk tributary land by the page's account; it dates no 1085 growth ('Established: 1041/1190') and does not mention Vilnius. Gazetteer test: of the 137 cells Cliopatria adds in 1085, 108 lie in its 1111 Jersika shape, 10 in Koknese and 15 in Minsk, so the growth is the land the 1101 splits below hand to Jersika, Koknese and Minsk. The year 1085 is still Cliopatria's only (confidence 1).

region.text: Vitebsk, the share of Sviatoslav Vseslavich

ledger.note: 1101: Vseslav dies on 24 April and Polotsk is divided; Vitebsk goes to Sviatoslav Vseslavich. 'Following the death of Vseslav of Polotsk in 1101, Polotsk was divided into six smaller principalities.' Cliopatria's Vitebsk row begins in 1111.

region.text: Minsk and its land, the share of Gleb Vseslavich, as Cliopatria draws the Principality of Minsk from 1111 (52,681 km2)

ledger.note: 1101: Minsk goes to Gleb Vseslavich. The Vseslav page lists Gleb as prince of Minsk and Vseslav's death on 24 April 1101; it describes no formal partition, the Vitebsk page dates the division ('Polotsk was divided into six smaller principalities each to be inherited by one of his six surviving sons'). The region is Cliopatria's Minsk shape of 1111 (52,681 km2), not a 60 km disc round the town: the five Cliopatria shapes of 1111 (Minsk, Drutsk, Vitebsk, Jersika, Koknese; 132,628 km2) cover 613 of the 619 cells of the 1085 Polotsk shape (133,005 km2) without overlapping each other. Cliopatria's Minsk row begins in 1111.

region.text: Drutsk and its land, the share of Rogvolod-Boris Vseslavich, as Cliopatria draws the Principality of Drutsk from 1111

ledger.note: 1101: Drutsk goes to Rogvolod-Boris Vseslavich. The Vseslav page: 'Rogvolod-Boris was prince of Drutsk' (some historians think Boris and Rogvolod were one man). Cliopatria's Drutsk row begins in 1111.

region.text: Jersika and its Latgalian land on the Daugava, as Cliopatria draws the Principality of Jersika from 1111 (23,422 km2)

ledger.note: 1101: Jersika passes out of Polotsk's direct rule when the principality is divided after Vseslav's death. The Principality of Polotsk page names Jersika and Koknese among the smaller fiefs ('Polotsk was splintered between various smaller fiefs'; 'the principality was divided between his surviving sons') and says the principalities of Jersika and Koknese conquered by the German crusaders in 1209 'had previously been under the control of Polotsk'. The year is the division's (Vitebsk page: 1101), not a date the page gives for Jersika; the Jersika page's infobox reads 'Established: 1041/1190' and has 'Preceded by: Principality of Polotsk', and Polotsk kept tributary rights until 1212. Cliopatria's Jersika row begins in 1111.

region.text: Koknese on the Daugava, as Cliopatria draws the Principality of Koknese from 1111 (2,162 km2)

ledger.note: 1101: Koknese passes out of Polotsk's direct rule with the division after Vseslav's death. The Principality of Polotsk page names Koknese with Jersika among the smaller fiefs and says that the principalities conquered by the crusaders in 1209 ('In 1209 German crusaders conquered the principalities of Jersika and Koknese') 'had previously been under the control of Polotsk'. The page dates neither fief's separation; the year is the division's (Vitebsk page: 1101). Cliopatria's Koknese row begins in 1111.

region.text: Polotsk with the middle Dvina and the Vitebsk lands, Cliopatria's post-1202 shape (34,385 km2)

ledger.note: 1127: Mstislav of Kiev makes war on Polotsk. 'In 1127, the prince of Kyiv, Mstislav Vladimirovich, began a war with the princes of Polotsk over trade routes'; the Mstislav page lists 'the princedom of Polotsk (1127; 1129)' among his wars. In 1129 he 'captured the three remaining sons of Vseslav' and sent them to Constantinople (Kievan Rus' page: 'By 1130, all descendants of Vseslav the Seer had been exiled to the Byzantine Empire'). The Vitebsk page gives the result in 1129: Mstislav 'annexed Polotsk and its vassals including Vitebsk' (see the contest_end and loss of 1129).

region.text: Polotsk with the middle Dvina and the Vitebsk lands, Cliopatria's post-1202 shape (34,385 km2)

ledger.note: 1129: Mstislav annexes Polotsk and the contest ends in Kiev's favour. The Vitebsk page: in 1129 Mstislav 'captured the three remaining sons of Vseslav' and 'annexed Polotsk and its vassals including Vitebsk'; the Kievan Rus' page: 'By 1130, all descendants of Vseslav the Seer had been exiled to the Byzantine Empire'. The Polotsk page's infobox reads the whole 1127-1132 as 'Vassal of Kievan Rus''; the dossier follows the Vitebsk page's 'annexed' for 1129-1132 and keeps 1127-1129 as the contest.

region.text: Polotsk proper, the 1202 core without the Vitebsk fief (the 1101 keyframe)

ledger.note: 1129: Polotsk proper passes to Kiev. 'annexed Polotsk and its vassals including Vitebsk' (Principality of Vitebsk page, 1129). The region is Polotsk without the Vitebsk fief; the page's 'including Vitebsk' means the Vitebsk land changed hands too, which belongs to the ledgers of principality-of-vitebsk and principality-of-kiev.

region.text: Polotsk proper, the 1202 core without the Vitebsk fief (the 1101 keyframe)

ledger.note: 1132: Polotsk is Vseslavichi land again. 'In 1132, the residents of Polotsk unhappy with the rule of' Svyatopolk Mstislavich 'invited Vasilko to claim the Principality of Polotsk'; Mstislav died in 1132 (Kievan Rus' page) and the exiled princes were 'allowed to return in 1139'. The Polotsk infobox ends the 'Vassal of Kievan Rus'' span in 1132.

region.text: the Vitebsk lands, a fief apart from 1101 to about 1195

ledger.note: 1165: the princes of Smolensk take Vitebsk. 'In 1165-1167 due to the feudal strife, the principality of Vitebsk was shortly acquired by the princes of Smolensk.' The princes' list has 'Smolensk rule (1167-1168)'.

region.text: the Vitebsk lands, a fief apart from 1101 to about 1195

ledger.note: 1168: Briachislav Vasilkovich recovers Vitebsk (the list: 'Briachislav Vasilkovich (1168-1175)'); 'Vitebsk later regained independence under Briachislav Vasilkovich.'

region.text: the Vitebsk lands, a fief apart from 1101 to about 1195

ledger.note: 1186: Vitebsk falls again under Smolensk's influence. 'In 1186, the principality of Vitebsk again fell under the influence of Smolensk,' which angered Polotsk and Chernigov.

region.text: the Vitebsk lands, a fief apart from 1101 to about 1195

ledger.note: 1195: Polotsk and its allies restore Vitebsk. The princes who 'in 1195 marched against the prince of Smolensk' then restored Vitebsk to Polotsk's rule; Polotsk and Vitebsk are one land again.

region.text: the Vitebsk lands, restored to Polotsk's rule

ledger.note: 1195: Vitebsk returns to Polotsk. The princes who 'in 1195 marched against the prince of Smolensk' restored the fief, and 'Vitebsk again fell under the rule of Polotsk' (Principality of Vitebsk page). This is the land split off in 1101 (the split with principality-of-vitebsk); the contest with Smolensk ends in the same year.

1307: Vytenis of Lithuania annexes Polotsk by force. 'Vytenis annexed the city by force in 1307'; the Principality page: 'It officially became part of Lithuania in 1307, though it retained some degree of local autonomy until the 1390s' and 'in 1240 Polotsk became a vassal of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania'. The Mongol invasion of 1237-1239 had passed it by. The Polotsk page: Vytenis 'annexed the city by military force in 1307, completing the process which the Lithuanian princes had begun in the 1250s.'

wars.name: Nemiga campaign and Vseslav's captivity
wars.outcome: The Yaroslavichi sacked Minsk and beat Vseslav on the Nemiga (3 March 1067); he was imprisoned, freed by the Kiev uprising of 1068, held Kiev for about seven months and 'finally secured Polotsk in 1071'.
wars.note: The Vseslav page dates the capture to June without a year; the Vitebsk and Principality pages are silent on 1067.

wars.name: Mstislav of Kiev's war on Polotsk

zones.text: Polotsk with the middle Dvina and the Vitebsk lands, Cliopatria's post-1202 shape (34,385 km2)

wars.outcome: Mstislav captured Vseslav's remaining sons in 1129 and exiled them to Constantinople; the Vitebsk page says he 'annexed Polotsk and its vassals including Vitebsk' (ledger loss 1129); the town invited Vasilko Sviatoslavich in 1132 (gain 1132) and the exiles returned in 1139. Polotsk page infobox: 'Vassal of Kievan Rus' (978-1001, 1127-1132)'.
wars.note: The Mstislav page lists the Polotsk wars as (1127; 1129) with no detail; the Vitebsk page has the rest. Polotsk page infobox: 'Vassal of Kievan Rus' (978-1001, 1127-1132)'.

wars.name: Smolensk's claims on Vitebsk

zones.text: the Vitebsk lands, a fief apart from 1101 to about 1195

wars.outcome: Smolensk held Vitebsk in 1165-1168 and again had influence over it from 1186; Polotsk and Chernigov princes marched against Smolensk in 1195 and restored Vitebsk to Polotsk's rule.
wars.note: Not a continuous war: two episodes, 1165-1168 and 1186-1195.

wars.name: German crusade on the Daugava
wars.outcome: 'In 1209 German crusaders conquered the principalities of Jersika and Koknese'; in 1212 Polotsk was forced 'to permit free travel to German merchants'; in 1227 'Smolensk ceded Polotsk by treaty to the city of Riga' (infobox: vassal of the Livonian Brothers of the Sword 1227-1240).
wars.note: The Polotsk core shape does not move; Jersika and Koknese have their own Cliopatria rows. The vassalage 1227-1240 belongs in livonian-brothers-of-the-sword's ledger.

wars.name: Lithuanian takeover of Polotsk
wars.outcome: Vassal of the Lithuanian princes from 1240; Tautvilas, Mindaugas's nephew, was given Polotsk in 1254 (Vitebsk page); annexed by force by Vytenis in 1307; autonomy to the 1390s.
wars.note: Polotsk escaped the Mongol invasion of 1237-1239 (Principality page) and paid no Mongol tribute (Polotsk page).

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line on the pages opened; the frontiers with Lithuanian, Latgalian and Livonian lands are approximate throughout.

notes: Pages opened (budget 5, used 5 plus the Kievan Rus' page shared with the group): Polotsk (the town), Principality of Polotsk, Vseslav of Polotsk, Mstislav I of Kiev (thin), Principality of Vitebsk. Cliopatria wikipedia field says 'Polotsk' (the town page); the dossier gives 'Principality of Polotsk', the right article. Start 1054 is the end of the rus dossier; the pages put the principality far earlier (862; Rogvolod 980; Vseslav 1044). End 1307 follows the pages; Cliopatria ends the row in 1249 and covers the core with Lithuania from 1250. Overlaps for the colour agent to settle: (1) Cliopatria's Vitebsk row 1111-1187 (34,385 km2) is the same shape as Polotsk 1202, so it is Polotsk-plus-Vitebsk, and Smolensk 1188-1201 holds those cells too; (2) 1250-1306 against Lithuania. Vassal events belong in the suzerains' dossiers, with counterpart principality-of-polotsky: livonian-brothers-of-the-sword 1227-1240 (infobox 'vassal of the Livonian Brothers of the Sword (1227-1240)'), grand-duchy-of-lithuania 1240-1307, and principality-of-kiev 1127-1132. Not on any page opened: the dates of the 1085 western reach, Lithuanian 1183 independence beyond a phrase, the Daugava lands' status. REPAIR 2026-10-31 (review eu-16-c): (1) the 1101 division now carries five splits (Vitebsk, Minsk as Cliopatria's 1111 shape, Drutsk, Jersika, Koknese), so the fall from 133,005 km2 is explained; the Jersika and Koknese splits are dated by the division, not by a page that names them (Principality of Polotsk page names them among the smaller fiefs). (2) Kiev's 1129 annexation is a loss (1129) and a gain (1132) with principality-of-kiev, region Polotsk proper; the page's 'including Vitebsk' means the Vitebsk fief was annexed too, which the principality-of-vitebsk and principality-of-kiev ledgers should show; the Polotsk infobox's 'Vassal of Kievan Rus' 1127-1132' is the other reading and is not used beyond the contest. (3) Vitebsk's 1195 return is a gain with principality-of-vitebsk. Pages opened for the repair: Principality of Polotsk, Principality of Vitebsk, Principality of Jersika (new, over the original budget of 5), Polotsk (town).
